notes.meaning: Paul shows that the most impressive speech is completely empty without Christian love. Even if a person could speak every human language or the exalted tongue of angels, a loveless heart turns that speech into nothing more than clanging noise. Genuine love for God and others is the only thing that gives our words and spiritual abilities real value.

differ.view: Some understand the tongues of angels as an actual heavenly prayer language given to believers by the Holy Spirit today.
The tongues of angels are understood as an impossible extreme used only to make a strong point, not a language humans can actually speak.

notes.meaning: Here Paul speaks of remarkable gifts like inspired preaching, knowing deep spiritual mysteries, and having enough faith to perform astounding miracles. Yet having all this ability without love leaves a person as an absolute zero in God's eyes. Spiritual power without a caring heart achieves nothing of eternal worth.

A person might give away every possession piece by piece to feed the poor, or even face death as a martyr. If those great sacrifices are done for selfish pride, personal honor, or public applause, they bring no heavenly reward at all. God values the sincere love of the heart far more than outward acts of sacrifice.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some ancient Greek manuscripts read that I may boast rather than to be burned, emphasizing that even giving up one's life is worthless if done for personal pride.

notes.meaning: True love proves itself through patient endurance and active kindness. It does not fly into a rage when hurt, but instead looks for ways to do good to others. Because love is content, it does not burn with jealousy over someone else's success, nor does it brag or swell up with pride.

Love treats everyone with respect, courtesy, and decency rather than acting in a rude or harsh way. It is not selfish, demanding its own advantage ahead of everyone else. It does not lose its temper easily, and it refuses to keep a mental record of injuries to use for future revenge.

Love finds no pleasure in wrongdoing or the moral failures of other people. It never secretly gloats when an enemy falls into sin or trouble. Instead, it rejoices whenever truth, justice, and holy living flourish.

Love protects others by drawing a quiet veil over their faults rather than spreading them abroad. It is ready to believe the best about people as far as honesty allows, and it never gives up hope for them. Through insults, trials, and hard times, love stands firm and keeps on bearing up.

Love is eternal and will never end or drop out of use. By contrast, gifts like prophecy, miraculous tongues, and supernatural knowledge are temporary tools given to build up the church for a time. When their earthly purpose is finished, they will fade away, but love will last forever.

differ.view: Miraculous gifts like tongues and prophecy were given only to establish the early church and ended after the apostles died.
All the miraculous gifts of the Spirit are intended to stay active in the church until Christ returns.

notes.meaning: Our present knowledge and inspired preaching give us only tiny glimpses into the great truths of God. When the final, perfect state arrives in eternity, all these incomplete and piecemeal helpers will come to an end. Just as the light of the sun makes starlight vanish, the full glory of heaven will replace our partial gifts.

differ.view: The perfect refers to the completed collection of the New Testament Scriptures, after which miraculous gifts were no longer needed.

notes.meaning: Paul compares life on earth to being an infant, and life in heaven to fully grown adulthood. A child talks in broken words, thinks simply, and reasons with childish notions, but gladly puts those things away when grown. In the same way, the church's earthly gifts are suited for this present age, but they will be outgrown in heaven.

Right now our view of heavenly things is indirect and dim, like looking at an image in a foggy, polished metal mirror. In eternity we will see God directly and openly, face to face. Our present knowledge is tiny and incomplete, but in heaven our understanding will be clear and direct, just as God clearly sees and knows us right now.

Faith, hope, and love stand together as the three essential virtues that outshine all temporary gifts. Yet love is the greatest of them because it reflects the very heart of God and brings blessing to everyone. While faith turns to open sight and hope is fulfilled in heaven, love will never cease, continuing its perfect work for all eternity.
